I’m not okay with people getting fat. It increases the costs of medical care for the rest of us. Obesity is 100% preventable.

[Direct medical cost of overweight and obesity in the United States - NIH](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2891924/) 

[Adult Obesity Causes and Consequences - CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/obesity/adult/causes.html) 

Obesity contributes to a wide array of other medical issues. This causes everyone else to pay higher insurance rates when obesity increases within the population.

I’m specifically talking about obesity here, BMI of 30+.  There are risk factors that contribute like genetics, medications, etc., but obesity is simply caused by too many calories and not enough activity. If you have a condition that puts you at an increased risk, there are options to counteract weight gain through nutrition, exercise, and behavioral changes. 

For the record this is nothing personal against fat people. I just fail to see any benefits to society at large when 40% of the US population is over consuming.
